profile.headline: Software Engineer at Uber
profile.summary:
I've always been passionate about software development, and exposure to Android and Backend development increased my love for it even more. I love to spend free time on teaching myself new skills to become a better engineer and team player. As a passionate, responsible, and diligent person, I always give 100% of my ability to achieve the highest results for any given tasks, in a timely manner.

Graduated from San Jose State University with a B.S. in Computer Science, I have 7+ years of experiences in various Android Development skills, backend development, as well as database management, and can utilize those skills to build and maintain fully responsive and functional web and mobile applications. I have great passion for learning new technologies and utilizing them to develop outstanding and life-changing products. I'm hoping to become a part of a tech company that has great and unique vision, where I can apply my knowledge to implement products that can change the world for the better.

projects.title: Foodie
projects.description:
Foodie is an Android application which allows users to share their favorite food and/or restaurants all over the world. 
MVP architectural design to improve separation of concern, code test-ability and maintainability.
Material Design elements and guidelines for great user experience design.
Firebase is used as the back-end server to store data for the Foodie application
Notifications for user interactions are also provided through Firebase Cloud Messaging and Cloud Functions.

projects.title: Alpha Fitness
projects.description:
This application utilizes the built-in accelerometer sensor in Android devices to compute workout information such as footsteps, calories burned, distanced traveled, etc.
During active workouts in landscape mode, the application displays a real time update of calories burned and step counts on a graph plotted using MPAndroidChart library, as well as the rate of maximum, minimum, and average minutes per mile. 
On portrait mode, a map showing the workout path will be displayed and updated in real time.
SQLite is used to keep a record of all workouts performed, and the data is saved locally to the device's internal storage.
Remote services and threads are utilized to keep the application running in the background, even in the case of the screen being turned off.
